comment: Every place a source is weaker than it looks. This package's top rung is empty: no manufacturer document for the S-DD1 is known to exist, so the entries here are about what stands in for one and how far it goes.

sources.reference: The S-DD1 decoder in snes9x 1.63, which produced every expected output in vectors.json and corpus.json.
sources.cartridges: Builds carrying tagged streams, which are not retail dumps. See the entry below.

divergences.referenceDoes: conformance/corpus.json describes its census as measured from real S-DD1 cartridges and records no provenance: no file names, no digests, no dates.
divergences.reasoning: conformance/extract.py finds a stream by searching for a four byte SDD1 tag. Measured on 2026-08-21 across a library of 7,578 images: the four retail cartridges that carry this chip, Star Ocean (Japan), Street Fighter Alpha 2 (USA) and (Europe), and Street Fighter Zero 2 (Japan), contain that tag zero times. The only builds that carry it are two modified Virtual Console re-releases, and they yield 5,630 streams spread evenly across all sixteen shapes, where the shipped census records 11,306 with 2,815 of them in a single shape. Neither the count nor the distribution can be reproduced from anything in that library, and a run of 2,815 streams all sharing one shape is what coincidental byte matches look like rather than what a game's data looks like. So the census cannot have been measured the way its own comment says, and part of it is probably not measuring streams at all. Since 2026-08-25 a census with full provenance exists beside it: conformance/cartridges.json records 55,023 streams found in Star Ocean by decoding rather than by searching for a tag, with the file names, four digests each and the date, and 238 distinct header bytes across all sixteen kinds. It does not replace conformance/corpus.json, which still carries the shipped vectors. Since 2026-08-30 a second census covers two more: conformance/indexed.json records 2,814 streams in Street Fighter Alpha 2, read from a stream table that is not in the cartridge at all. The re-release of the same game replaces the eight bytes at each stream start with the literal SDD1 and a four byte destination, and those destinations run forward across the whole image, so the gap between two of them is a decompressed length and the tag's offset is where the stream begins. That is an offset and a length per stream, which is what was asked for. Whether a stream starts at the tag or at the byte after it was decided by the header bytes rather than assumed: at the tag they are 52 distinct values across 8 of the 16 kinds with 88 percent in one, and at the byte after they are all 256 values spread evenly across all 16, which is what reading data that is not a header looks like. The USA and Europe cartridges give identical counts from the same table. Street Fighter Zero 2 (Japan) is not covered: the same table read against it gives 167 distinct headers across all 16 kinds, so that build holds its streams elsewhere. Three of the four cartridges now have a census with provenance.
divergences.wouldSettleIt: A stream table for Street Fighter Zero 2 (Japan), which is the one retail cartridge with neither a decompressed control nor an indexing re-release. Failing that, regenerating conformance/corpus.json from a named source with its digest recorded, and saying outright that the source is not a retail dump.
divergences.doesItAffectTheDecoder: Not directly. The census describes which shapes real data uses; it does not decide what the decoder does with one. Every shape is exercised by the random vectors regardless. What it does affect is the claim that this decoder has been run against the shapes hardware actually drives, and that claim is currently unsupported.

divergences.referenceDoes: Produces the bytes the corpus and the vector file compare against. It is no longer the only thing this decoder has been measured against, and since 2026-08-31 it is no longer the only lineage either.
divergences.reasoning: It was true that there was no other source, and it is no longer. This decoder is also measured against a retail cartridge, against an expansion somebody else produced from one, against streams a third party's encoder emitted, and now against a Capcom prototype of the Japanese cartridge dated 1996-09-15 that predates the compression. That last one is the first witness that does not descend from Andreas Naive's research: 242 streams this decoder expands from the retail cartridge appear verbatim in the prototype, 311,264 bytes in total, which makes them Capcom's own input to Capcom's own compressor. The decoder has been shown to invert the thing rather than to agree with an account of it.
divergences.wouldSettleIt: A recording taken off a real S-DD1, which would move this to the top of the ladder. The prototype settles the lineage objection for the streams it covers and cannot settle the rest, because it is a different build and most of its data differs.

divergences.documentSays: Nothing. Neither Ricoh nor Nintendo published a datasheet for the S-DD1.
divergences.reasoning: The top rung of this family's authority ladder is empty for this part, which is worth stating rather than leaving a reader to infer it from the absence of quotes. Every constant in hardware.json carries verified false for this reason and not because anybody doubts the value.
divergences.wouldSettleIt: A Ricoh or Nintendo datasheet, or a die photograph.

divergences.referenceDoes: Decodes a whole stream in one call, as this package does.
divergences.reasoning: How long the chip takes, and whether a console reading the decompressed data can outrun it, is not modelled. On real hardware that question decides whether a game has to wait, and nothing on this machine can answer it.
divergences.wouldSettleIt: A measurement on a real cartridge, or a datasheet.
